claims.explanation: Levocetirizine is a selective HRH1 antagonist, and its antiproliferative effects in cancer cell lines likely depend on HRH1 expression, which can drive autocrine/paracrine growth signaling in some tumors. The pattern of sensitivity is not explained by a single common mutation; instead, HRH1-high lines with RAS/RAF/PI3K pathway activation may be more dependent on histamine signaling, while HRH1-low lines are protected. The virtual cell data showing chlorphenamine (another histamine receptor antagonist) as a top transcriptional match supports an on-target mechanism.
